explanation: A hundred and fifty years, and the weakest type. The traffic did not organise the rising and nothing about it made a successful revolution likely — the cited account calls it the only slave rebellion known to have founded a state free of slavery and ruled by former captives, which is a statement about how rarely this happened. What the traffic supplied was the demographic fact the revolution was made out of: an enslaved majority, overwhelmingly African-born, in a colony held by a small white population.
